## Quarto

Quarto enables you to weave together content and executable code into a finished document. To learn more about Quarto see <https://quarto.org>.

## Running Code

When you click the **Render** button a document will be generated that includes both content and the output of embedded code. You can embed code like this:

```{r}
1 + 1
```

You can add options to executable code like this

```{r}
#| echo: false
2 * 2
```

The `echo: false` option disables the printing of code (only output is displayed).

```{r}
# ---- Setup ----
n <- 100
p <- 1/6

# ---- Step 1: Mean and SD of the null distribution ----
mu <- n * p
sigma <- sqrt(n * p * (1 - p))
cat("Mean:", mu, " SD:", sigma, "\n")

# ---- Step 2: Normal approximation cutoffs (z = 1.96 for alpha = 0.05, two-tailed) ----
z <- qnorm(0.975)  # 1.96
lower_approx <- mu - z * sigma
upper_approx <- mu + z * sigma
cat("Normal approx cutoffs:", lower_approx, upper_approx, "\n")

# ---- Step 3: Exact binomial tail probabilities for candidate cutoffs ----
# P(X <= k) for a few candidate lower cutoffs
for (k in 8:11) {
  cat("P(X <=", k, ") =", pbinom(k, n, p), "\n")
}

# P(X >= k) for a few candidate upper cutoffs
for (k in 23:26) {
  cat("P(X >=", k, ") =", 1 - pbinom(k - 1, n, p), "\n")
}

# ---- Step 4: Actual Type I error rate for chosen rejection region (X<=9 or X>=25) ----
alpha_actual <- pbinom(9, n, p) + (1 - pbinom(24, n, p))
cat("Actual alpha for cutoffs (9, 25):", alpha_actual, "\n")

# ---- Step 5: Check the original 15-25 boundary (shows why it's miscalibrated) ----
alpha_original <- 1 - (pbinom(25, n, p) - pbinom(14, n, p))
cat("Actual alpha for cutoffs (15, 25):", alpha_original, "\n")

# ---- Step 6: Power calculations for various true biases ----
# Using the calibrated rejection region: reject if X<=9 or X>=25
p_alt <- c(0.20, 0.22, 0.25, 0.30)
power <- sapply(p_alt, function(pa) {
  pbinom(9, n, pa) + (1 - pbinom(24, n, pa))
})
data.frame(true_p = p_alt, power = power)
```

```{r}
n <- 100      # number of rolls
p <- 1/6      # null hypothesis: probability of rolling a 6 on a fair die

# Rejection region: reject H0 (call the die unfair) if X <= 9 or X >= 25

# Lower tail: P(X <= 9)
lower_tail <- pbinom(9, size = n, prob = p)
cat("P(X <= 9)  =", lower_tail, "\n")

# Upper tail: P(X >= 25)  =  1 - P(X <= 24)
upper_tail <- 1 - pbinom(24, size = n, prob = p)
cat("P(X >= 25) =", upper_tail, "\n")

# Type I error rate = sum of both tails (mutually exclusive events)
alpha_actual <- lower_tail + upper_tail
cat("Actual Type I error rate =", alpha_actual, "\n")
```
